Jimmy says to Pa, he says, 'Come along, Joe, I got the greatest bunch of murd-erers of English into the club you ever seen,' he says, 'and tonight the Honorable Wallace Fixem, Minister of Public Works, is going to attend our inaggeral meetin',' he says, 'and give us a spiel.'

arxiv-2103-05650.title: Phonon Hall viscosity from phonon-spinon interactions
arxiv-2103-05650.creator: Yunchao Zhang, Yanting Teng, Rhine Samajdar, Subir Sachdev, Mathias S. Scheurer
arxiv-2103-05650.description: Abstract Motivated by experimental observations, Samajdar et al. [Nature Physics 15 , 1290 (2019)] have proposed that the insulating Néel state in the parent compounds of the cuprates is proximate to a quantum phase transition to a state in which Néel order coexists with semion topological order.

arxiv-2307-12821.title: On the transverse stability of smooth solitary waves in a two-dimensional Camassa–Holm equation
arxiv-2307-12821.creator: Anna Geyer, Yue Liu, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky
arxiv-2307-12821.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Anna Geyer, Yue Liu, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky. We consider the propagation of smooth solitary waves in a two-dimensional generalization of the Camassa–Holm equation. We show that transverse perturbations to one-dimensional solitary waves behave similarly to the KP-II theory.

arxiv-2510-02862.title: Imprints of dynamic ﬂuidization on dilepton production
arxiv-2510-02862.creator: \firstname Renan \lastname Góes-Hirayama \fnsep, \firstname Zuzana \lastname Paulínyová, \firstname Joscha \lastname Egger, \firstname Iurii \lastname Karpenko, \firstname Hannah \lastname Elfner
arxiv-2510-02862.description: Abstract We present a newly developed hybrid hadronic transport + hydrodynamics framework geared towards heavy ion collisions (HICs) at low to intermediate beam energies, and report on the resulting excitation function of dileptons. In this range of energies, it is unclear how to properly initialize the hydrodynamic evolution.

arxiv-2512-09995.title: Searches for electroweak states at future plasma wakefield colliders
arxiv-2512-09995.creator: So Chigusa, Simon Knapen, Toby Opferkuch, Inbar Savoray, Christiane Scherb, and Weishuang Linda Xu
arxiv-2512-09995.description: Abstract We quantify the discovery potential of future multi-TeV plasma wakefield colliders for new electroweak multiplets. We include beam–beam effects through realistic luminosity spectra, comparing five collider configurations: e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} and e − ​ e − e^{-}e^{-} machines with round- and flat-beams, and a γ ​ γ \gamma\gamma collider.

pmc-10591382.title: Bifidobacterium bifidum and Lactobacillus paracasei alleviate sarcopenia and cognitive impairment in aged mice by regulating gut microbiota-mediated AKT, NF-κB, and FOXO3a signaling pathways
pmc-10591382.creator: Ji-Su Baek, Yoon-Jung Shin, Xiaoyang Ma, Hee-Seo Park, Yun-Ha Hwang, Dong-Hyun Kim
pmc-10591382.description: Sarcopenia is closely associated with gut dysbiosis. Probiotics alleviate gut dysbiosis. Therefore, we selected probiotics Lactobacillus paracasei P62 (Lp) and Bifidobacterium bifidum P61 (Bb), which suppressed muscle RING-finger protein-1 (MuRF1) expression and NF-κB activation in C2C12 cells, and examined their effects on muscle mass loss and dysfunction in aged mice.

pmc-11582772.title: Strengthening Africa's response to Mpox (monkeypox): insights from historical outbreaks and the present global spread
pmc-11582772.creator: David B. Olawade, Ojima Z. Wada, Sandra Chinaza Fidelis, Oluwafemi S. Oluwole, Chibuike S. Alisi, Nifemi F. Orimabuyaku, Aanuoluwapo Clement David-Olawade
pmc-11582772.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Mpox, formerly known as Monkeypox, is a viral zoonotic disease endemic to Central and West Africa that has posed significant public health challenges since its identification in 1970. Despite decades of experience in managing outbreaks, the 2022–2024 Mpox outbreaks exposed substantial gaps in global preparedness and response, leading the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) in 2022.

pmc-11677434.title: Real-Time Emotion Recognition for Improving the Teaching–Learning Process: A Scoping Review
pmc-11677434.creator: Cèlia Llurba, Ramon Palau, Yanfeng Li
pmc-11677434.description: Emotion recognition (ER) is gaining popularity in various fields, including education. The benefits of ER in the classroom for educational purposes, such as improving students’ academic performance, are gradually becoming known. Thus, real-time ER is proving to be a valuable tool for teachers as well as for students. However, its feasibility in educational settings requires further exploration.

pmc-12597399.title: Racial disparities in hepatocellular carcinoma: a TCGA-based gene expression study of Caucasian and Asian populations
pmc-12597399.creator: Muhammad Rezki Rasyak, Sri Jayanti, Cyrollah Disoma, Bens Pardamean, Caecilia Sukowati
pmc-12597399.description: Aim:Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) displays both shared and ethnicity-specific molecular characteristics. Using transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), we compared gene expression profiles between Asian and Caucasian HCC patients.Methods:Gene expression profiles were analyzed using the PyDESeq2 implementation of DESeq2, applying size factor normalization and dispersion estimation.

pmc-12731612.title: Cognitive Mechanisms Explaining the Relationship Between Post-Traumatic Stress and Post-Traumatic Growth in Survivors of Breast Cancer
pmc-12731612.creator: Vida Mirabolfathi, Fatemeh Ayoubi, Amirreza Nouri, Alireza Moradi, Laura Jobson, Nazanin Derakshan
pmc-12731612.description: Simple SummaryBreast cancer is a life-threatening and traumatic experience that leaves women with distress and anxiety for many years. However, research shows it is possible to grow from trauma in meaningful and adaptive ways. The current investigation attempted to identify the cognitive mechanisms underlying trauma and growth, which are involved in resilience and adaptation. Three important findings emerged.

pmc-13550935.title: Programmed ventricular stimulation for risk stratification in symptomatic athletes with nonischemic left ventricular scar and preserved ejection fraction
pmc-13550935.creator: Luigi Sciarra, Fabrizio Ricci, Elena Cavarretta, Zefferino Palamà, Alessio Borrelli, Mauro Di Roma, Leonardo Pignalosa, Federico Zanin, Daniele Falco, Giulia Renda, Cesare Mantini, Sabina Gallina, Francesco Brancati, Silvio Romano, Antonio Scarà
pmc-13550935.description: AimsNon-ischaemic left ventricular (LV) scar is increasingly recognized in athletes with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and may represent a substrate for malignant ventricular arrhythmias. The role of electrophysiological study (EPS) with programmed ventricular stimulation (PVS) for risk stratification in this population remains unclear.

pmc-13674150.title: Target‐Engagement Prediction From Molecular Structure, In Vitro and Animal Data: A Tutorial for Early Assessment of Clinical Drug Exposure and Therapeutic/Adverse Potential Using the ANDROMEDA and PLATO Software on the InSilicoTrials Platform
pmc-13674150.creator: Niccolò Totis, Fianne Sips, Simona Catozzi, Marc‐Antonio Bisotti, Pauline Bambury, Sofia Stathopoulos, Vincenzo Carbone, Luca Emili, Mario Torchia, Valentina Belgiovine, Fulvio Ciriaco, Orazio Nicolotti, Urban Fagerholm, Candice N Baker, J Matthew Mahoney, Daniel Röshammar, the CARDIOVERSE Project
pmc-13674150.description: The target‐engagement predictor, implemented within the InSilicoTrials cloud‐based, AI‐powered platform for model‐informed drug discovery and development, enables early exploration of time‐dependent pharmacological responses. Predictions can be generated using inputs ranging from molecular structure to in vitro, animal, and clinical data. Scaling and translation across species are supported, accounting for differences in body size and plasma protein binding.
